strategy.title: China's Space Program: A 2021 Perspective (State Council Information Office white paper)
strategy.status: published (January 2022); the stated five-year horizon has run; no successor white paper located in this run
strategy.horizon: 'In the next five years' (white paper text, 2022); no end year stated.
strategy.owner: State Council Information Office (publisher); CNSA (civil space implementation).
strategy.summary: The white paper reviews achievements since 2016 (BeiDou, high-resolution Earth observation, completion of the third lunar step, early space-station construction, Tianwen-1) and sets main tasks for the next five years, including law-based governance. On 26 Nov 2025 the CNSA released a two-year action plan to back commercial space firms and widen international cooperation. On 8 May 2026 the State Council's 2026 legislative plan listed a space law draft among items to prepare for NPC Standing Committee submission.
strategy.budget: No budget or funding figure appears in the full white paper text (searched for budget and funding terms; none found). The CNSA's Nov 2025 plan announces a national commercial space development fund with no amount in the text read. No consolidated national space budget was located.
goals: Integrate space science, technology and applications while pursuing the new development philosophy (white paper, next five years)
Promote law-based governance: speed up formulation of a national space law (white paper, Sec. 5)
Back commercial space firms and expand international cooperation over two years (CNSA action plan, Nov 2025)
Open national ground facilities to commercial users and create a commercial space development fund (CNSA action plan)
strategy.law: No national space law in force located. The white paper commits to speed up formulation of a national space law (Jan 2022). The State Council's 2026 plan lists a space law draft as preparatory for NPC Standing Committee submission (8 May 2026); no draft has been submitted in the sources read.

strategy.summary: Executive Order 14369, dated 18 December 2025 and published in the Federal Register on 23 December 2025, sets national space priorities: returning Americans to the Moon by 2028 through Artemis, initial elements of a lunar outpost by 2030, and a space security strategy to be implemented by the APNSA with the Secretary of War within 180 days (Sec. 3(d)). It supersedes and revokes EO 14056 (National Space Council) and revises Space Policy Directive 3 on space traffic management (Sec. 4).
strategy.budget: The order sets no appropriation. The NASA FY2027 request is USD 18,829.1 million (NASA budget request summary, April 2026, 'NASA Total' row), against FY2026 at 24,438.3 million in the same row; column labels are not in the text extract. Congress passed continuing appropriations (P.L. 119-103, approved 2 Sept 2026) that expire 11 Dec 2026; the NASA rate under that Act was not stated in the sections read. The FY2027 Space Force request (about USD 71 billion, secondary press only) is not proved from an official budget document.
goals: Return Americans to the Moon by 2028 through the Artemis Program (Sec. 2(a)(i))
Establish initial elements of a permanent lunar outpost by 2030 (Sec. 2(a)(ii))
Implement a space security strategy within 180 days, led by the APNSA with the Secretary of War (Sec. 3(d))
Reform space acquisition at Commerce and NASA within 180 days (Sec. 3(c))
strategy.law: Executive order, not statute. EO 14369 is in the Federal Register (Vol. 90, No. 244, 23 Dec 2025, from the Dec 18, 2025 order). The statutes cited in the seed (National Aeronautics and Space Act 1958; Commercial Space Launch Act 1984) were not opened in this run and are not claimed here.

strategy.title: Política Nacional Espacial
strategy.horizon: Not stated in the policy text read.
strategy.owner: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation (the Consejo de Política Espacial it presides)
strategy.summary: Approved by Supreme Decree No. 30 of 4 July 2024 (Diario Oficial, Decree 28 of 2025), cleared by the Comptroller General on 26 March 2025 per the MinCiencia PDF cover. It sets two central objectives: sustainable development of national space capabilities (research, advanced technology, talent and international cooperation) and integrated management of space for national security and socioeconomic progress. It has six strategic axes: cooperation and linkage with society; talent management; innovation and development; sustainable development; security and national sovereignty; and territorial planning. The Air Force's National Satellite System and the national space centre are the main operational vehicles named in the 2025 decree.
strategy.budget: No consolidated public space budget is stated in the policy text or in Decree 28 of 2025. Funding runs through ministry lines in the annual budget law (seed statement; not verified in the budget law).
goals: Sustainable development of national space capabilities in research, innovation and advanced technology
Talent formation for the space sector
Integrated management of space for national security and socioeconomic progress
Connection and exploration of the whole national territory with national space systems
International cooperation and linkage with society
strategy.law: No dedicated national space law was found in the sources opened. Ley 21.105, art. 4 m), which creates the Ministry of Science, gives it the duty to promote national space activity, coordinated with the Ministry of Defence (quoted in Decree 28 of 2025).

strategy.title: Programa Espacial Mexicano 2026-2030
strategy.owner: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT), with the Agencia Espacial Mexicana as technical authority
strategy.summary: Published in the DOF on 4 June 2026 under the ATDT as issuing body. It is aligned with the Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030 and the ATDT sectoral programme. Initial projects: a new national telecommunications satellite to connect remote localities; a constellation of small Earth observation satellites for civil protection, environment, agriculture and territorial planning; a national centre to process satellite imagery; training of specialists; and international cooperation, including ITU coordination of orbital positions and spectrum rights. It follows a period in which the AEM was restructured under the ATDT and left without a titular head (per March 2026 reporting).
strategy.budget: No dedicated budget figure for the 2026-2030 programme is stated in the programme text. Expansión (8 Jan 2026) reports the 2026 federal budget allocation to the AEM as 46,755 millones de pesos, a 33.1% cut from 69,950 million in 2025. The unit reading is unresolved: the seed's 'MXN 46.8 million' differs from the printed figure.
goals: Build a new national telecommunications satellite to connect remote localities
Deploy a constellation of small Earth observation satellites for civil protection, environment, agriculture, security and territorial planning
Create a national centre to process and analyse satellite imagery from national and commercial systems
Train Mexican specialists for the space sector
Link Mexico to the international space sector and strengthen management of orbital positions and spectrum rights at the ITU
strategy.law: No comprehensive national space activities law was found in the sources opened. The Ley que crea la Agencia Espacial Mexicana (DOF 30 Jul 2010) creates the AEM as a decentralised public body; its 2010 sector reference (Secretaría de Comunicaciones y Transportes) is superseded by the ATDT reform as stated in the 2026 programme. Constitutional basis: CPEUM arts. 26 and 28, as cited in the programme.

strategy.title: Exploration, Imagination, Innovation: A New Space Strategy for Canada
strategy.status: under revision (a replacement is being prepared; a Special Adviser on Space was appointed 21 Oct 2026)
strategy.horizon: No fixed end date in the 2019 document; dated commitments include the ESA agreement to 2030 and LEAP funding over five years
strategy.owner: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (Minister of Industry), delivered largely through the Canadian Space Agency
strategy.summary: The 2019 strategy names space a strategic national asset and sets five priorities, the first being Canada's contribution to the US-led Lunar Gateway. It commits CAD 1.9 billion to an AI-enabled deep-space robotic system, CAD 150 million over five years to the Lunar Exploration Accelerator Program, and renews the ESA cooperation agreement to 2030. CP24 reported on 21 Oct 2026 that the Minister of Industry described a new space strategy in preparation at SpaceBound 2026, and the Prime Minister named astronaut Jeremy Hansen as Special Adviser on Space on 21 Oct 2026. No replacement strategy text has been published in the sources opened.
strategy.budget: The 2019 strategy commits CAD 1.9 billion to the Gateway robotic system and CAD 150 million over five years to LEAP; a 2018 announcement (cited in the strategy) provided CAD 100 million over five years for LEO broadband. National Defence committed CAD 200 million for a 10-year launch pad lease and CAD 105 million in Launch the North grants in March 2026. No replacement strategy budget is published.
goals: Ensure Canada remains a leading spacefaring nation by joining the Lunar Gateway mission
Inspire the next generation of Canadians to reach for the stars
Harness space to solve everyday challenges for Canadians
Position Canada's commercial space sector to grow the economy and create jobs
Ensure Canada's leadership in acquiring and using space-based data
strategy.law: No comprehensive national space act. The Canadian Space Agency Act (S.C. 1990, c. 13; consolidated version current to 30 Sep 2026) applies. Commercial launch is handled case by case under the interim approach announced in January 2023. Bill C-28 (Canadian Space Launch Act) would amend the Aeronautics Act; its status is unverified in the primary record. ISED published a consultation on a new Space Act on 20 Oct 2026 (announced 22 Oct); comments are due 21 Dec 2026 per a law-firm summary.

strategy.budget: Seed figure, not re-proved: Phase III expected cost NT$25.1 billion (about US$814 million) for 2019 to 2028; TASA annual budget about NT$3.7 billion in 2023 and NT$4.4 billion in 2024. No current (2026) budget figure proved in this run.
goals: Deploy the eight-satellite FORMOSAT-8 optical constellation by 2031; FS-8B expected to launch in the first quarter of 2027 (Taipei Times, 16 Oct 2026)

strategy.summary: Decision 169/QD-TTg, issued 4 Feb 2021 by the Prime Minister, promulgates the strategy to 2030 and succeeds the 2006 national strategy. It targets a mid-level position in Southeast Asia by 2030 (VGP, 13 Mar 2026), replacement of the VINASAT-1 and VINASAT-2 telecom satellites, mastery of small high-resolution Earth observation satellites and a larger space workforce. At the 13 Mar 2026 inauguration of the Vietnam National Space Center the government restated the targets and said it is moving toward a national space law.
strategy.budget: No consolidated national space budget proved in this run (seed claim, absence not re-proved). Replace the VINASAT-1 and VINASAT-2 telecommunications satellites (Decision 169 text)

Upgrade about 10 specialised laboratories and develop about 5 space science groups and 15 space technology groups (Decision 169 text)

strategy.title: National Space Plan 2026-2032 (Národní kosmický plán 2026-2032)
strategy.owner: Government of the Czech Republic; drafted under the Ministry of Transport and administered by the Ministry of Industry and Trade since 1 March 2026
strategy.summary: Approved by the government on 22 October 2025 as the fourth national space plan. Vision: the Czech Republic as an active, internationally recognised space actor. Four priority areas: (1) strategic lines and competence platforms, (2) promising technologies, (3) the supporting space ecosystem, (4) institutionalisation of space activities, including a target of a Czech Space Agency by the end of 2032.
strategy.budget: Indicative financing table (Annex 6, mil. CZK): total 3,170 in 2026 and 2027, then 2,370 a year for 2028-2032. Mandatory ESA activities 400 a year (paid from MŠMT); optional ESA programmes minimum 1,470 a year; the ESA framework project 1,300 in 2026 and 2027 including the ISS mission (800 a year in those years). Government Resolution No. 365 of 21 May 2025 provides for a CZK 1,600 million ESA contribution for the mission in 2026-2027. Amounts are indicative and depend on the CZK/EUR rate.
goals: Define strategic lines of development and create competence platforms (priority area 1)
Support perspective space technologies (priority area 2)
Strengthen the supporting space ecosystem and use of space data (priority area 3)
Institutionalise space activities: transform VZLÚ and establish a Czech Space Agency by end-2032 (priority area 4)
strategy.law: No national space act found in this run. The plan text contains no reference to a space act. The e-Sbírka legal database was NOT checked in this run, so the absence is provisional (flagged).

strategy.title: Hungary's Space Strategy (English title on the 2021 government PDF; Hungarian title not verified)
strategy.status: under revision (announced; no government decision located)
strategy.horizon: Targets to 2030; first phase 2021-2025; long-term vision 15-20 years (strategy text).
strategy.owner: Government of Hungary. Prepared under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (responsible 2018-Dec 2023). Renewal now assigned by ministerial statement to the Ministry of Science and Technology (2026).
strategy.summary: The government's first space strategy (2021) sets three strategic goals: use space to drive innovation and growth; strengthen Hungary's international role and coordination; build the knowledge base, skills and infrastructure. Its short-term action plan includes flagship items such as the HUNOR research-astronaut mission. On 26 June 2026 the minister named renewal as his first task and said no government decision had yet been taken. On 20 Oct 2026 the ministry said it had drafted a new science-policy and innovation strategy; this is not a space strategy.
strategy.budget: No appropriated space budget line located. The 2021 strategy estimated HUF 30-35 billion of additional state expenditure over 2021-2025 beyond ESA commitments (an estimate, not an appropriation) and HUF 10-15 billion to 2030. The 2027 draft budget summaries opened (kormany.hu/koltsegvetes and two 2027 news items) show no space line; the full bill was not opened. A Sept 2026 report says space contracts linked to predecessor ministries total about HUF 820-850 billion, some to 2040, and are under review.
goals: Use the space sector to drive innovation and sustainable growth in the national economy
Strengthen Hungary's international role, external connections and coordination structures in space
Build the knowledge, skills and infrastructure base the space sector needs
Flagship items: HUNOR research-astronaut mission, individual satellite programme, ground station capacity, radiation testing laboratory
strategy.law: No national space law or space agency law in force located. On 26 June 2026 the government said it would found a space agency and adopt a space law (Infostart); no bill or government decision was located.

Secure at least 5 commercial space contracts outside ESA and EU programmes (seed; not fully re-read)
Double above-threshold Horizon Europe space proposals and place Latvian researchers in ESA science mission teams (seed; not fully re-read)
Launch at least five new Earth observation or navigation services and integrate space capabilities into at least five non-space companies (seed; not fully re-read)

government.notes: Mongolia has no space agency. Civil space policy sits in the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications, which hosts the secretariat of the National Space Council (2022 MoU). The national communications satellite (Chinggis Sat) was presented through the Cabinet, National Security Council and Parliament in 2024 and is financed partly by State Budget amendments (15 percent) and partly under France-Mongolia arrangements. The Prime Minister has been Nyam-Osoryn Uchral since parliamentary confirmation on 30 March 2026. Frequent prime-ministerial changes since 2025 and the Vision 2050 policy are seed claims not re-proved here. The mddic parent link to Cabinet is not re-proved.

strategy.summary: A 10-year national programme led by MTCIT under Royal Decree 90/2020 to make Oman a regional gateway for space applications. It rests on four pillars (economic diversification, national security, capacity building, environmental stewardship) and 14 flagship projects (11 core, 3 non-core) with 8 quick wins.
strategy.budget: No public space budget figure was found. goals: Position Oman as a regional gateway for space applications and services

Build national capacity through training, CubeSat programmes and startup support
Strengthen governance and regulation, including a dedicated space law
Attract private investment into the space sector
strategy.law: No space law in force. MTCIT has begun drafting an Omani Space Law and supporting regulations (Oman Observer, 27 Sep 2026); no enactment date has been announced. Launch airspace is governed by Civil Aviation Authority regulations (secondary report).

strategy.owner: Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI); implemented by SANSA
strategy.summary: The National Space Strategy directs the South African Space Programme (SANSA plan 2025). The strategy goals include a competitive domestic space industry, export markets, government decision support from space data, and human capital. SANSA's 2025–2030 plan sets six outcomes and sits under the NSS. The 2008 National Space Policy (dti) sets the policy frame under the Space Affairs Act. goals: Build a competitive domestic space industry, including small and medium satellite manufacturing (NSS goal, SANSA plan 2025)
Develop an export market for South African satellites, products and services (NSS goal, SANSA plan 2025)
Integrate space-based and ground data for government decision support (NSS goal, SANSA plan 2025)
Develop geospatial, communications, timing and positioning applications (NSS goal, SANSA plan 2025)
Build human capital in space science and engineering (NSS goal, SANSA plan 2025)
Partner with spacefaring nations and extend space benefits across Africa (NSS goal, SANSA plan 2025)

strategy.title: Space Strategy 2030 (Avaruusstrategia 2030)
strategy.owner: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment with the Finnish Space Committee
strategy.summary: Renewed national space strategy, published as Publications of the Finnish Government 2025:8 (January 2025). Vision: 'Finland 2030: World’s most advanced space operating environment, which generates benefits for society as a whole.' Four objectives: utilisation of space services across society; a streamlined and secure operating environment; capabilities to produce and use space services; and an active international role. Prepared by a working group under the Finnish Space Committee's Secretary-General and steered by the Committee. Status 'in force' reflects the 2025 publication; no repeal was found in this run.
strategy.budget: No separate budget figure in the strategy text; it states that the measures are defined against economic constraints and available resources. Seed figures (EUR 233m ESA CM25; EUR 158m ICEYE SAR contract) are NOT re-proved and are in flags only.
goals: Utilisation: use space services to streamline and secure activities in all areas of society
Operating environment: Finland as an inspiring, secure and predictable environment for space actors
Capabilities: Finland can produce and utilise space services and has the capabilities to do so
International cooperation: Finland as a reliable, sought-after and active actor in the space sector
strategy.law: Act on Space Activities (Laki avaruustoiminnasta 63/2018), in force since January 2018; the Act on Earth Stations and Certain Radars (96/2023) is also cited in the strategy. A draft government proposal (VN/9441/2025) to move licensing to Traficom is a consultation draft (PIA statement 23.2.2026); not enacted per any opened source.

strategy.owner: Government of Sweden, Ministry of Education and Research (Utbildningsdepartementet); implemented by the Swedish National Space Agency
strategy.summary: Government communication of 9 May 2018 setting long-term strategic goals for Swedish space activity: benefit to society with national security safeguarded, international cooperation, use of space data, legislation, industry and research. Supplemented by the first defence and security strategy for space (4 Jul 2024) and a licensing overhaul under preparation (May 2026 assignment toward a new space law). Sweden did not join ESA's European Resilience from Space element at the November 2025 ministerial, on government instruction, according to the agency budget submission.
strategy.budget: ESA: EUR 305 million (1.36 per cent) subscribed at the November 2025 ministerial, per the agency budget submission. Agency requested minimum SEK 2,080,756 thousand for 2027 and SEK 2,946,356 thousand for 2029 under appropriation 3:4 (proposal). Spring 2026 amending budget: SEK 400 million total to the agency and SSC Space AB, of which SEK 14 million for licensing (government release, 12 May 2026). Military: SEK 1 billion for Armed Forces space capability 2024–2032 (decision 4 Oct 2024). Split of the SEK 400 million (SEK 386 million equity to SSC) and the January 2026 SEK 1.3 billion military satellite package are not proved.
goals: Secure Swedish freedom of action in and access to space (Skr. 2017/18:259, section 2.1)
Prevent the placement of weapons in space and keep space from becoming an arena for conflict
Use space and space services peacefully for human welfare and sustainable development, with transparency and openness
Contribute to international rules for space activity, including debris management
Use space data across society and keep ESA and EU participation predictable (per the strategy text)
Use synergies between civil and military space activity, with defence and security aspects considered
strategy.law: Act on Space Activities (Lag 1982:963 om rymdverksamhet), in force, issued 18 Nov 1982 and amended up to SFS 2021:1025 (riksdagen.se register). A new Swedish space law is in preparation: in May 2026 the agency was assigned to prepare a new licensing organisation as a first step toward a new space law. No bill was proved on the fetched pages.

strategy.title: Austrian Space Strategy 2030+ (Österreichische Weltraumstrategie 2030+: Mensch, Klima, Wirtschaft: Weltraum ist für ALLE da)
strategy.owner: Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK) in the 2021 imprint; implementation with the FFG Aeronautics and Space Agency. Current successor for space (BMIMI) per the 27 Oct 2026 government list and the BMIMI space section; formal transfer of the strategy not proved.
strategy.summary: The 2021 strategy frames space as a tool for people, climate and the economy, with six goals to 2030 and beyond. It is implemented by the lead ministry with the FFG aeronautics and space agency. Austria acts mainly through ESA and EU programmes, complemented by the ASAP national applications programme (about 800 projects and about EUR 130 million since 2002, per the 2021 text). A periodic implementation report and a monitoring concept with indicators are foreseen. No successor strategy was found in this pass.
strategy.budget: ASAP: about 800 projects and about EUR 130 million since 2002 (2021 strategy text). ESA: the seed's figure of EUR 340 million subscribed at the November 2025 ministerial is NOT proved: the November 2025 ministerial is confirmed on ESA's page, but the FFG source is blocked and no Austrian figure was retrieved.
goals: Ziel 1: Sustainable development on Earth and in space (Nachhaltige Entwicklung)
Ziel 2: A competitive space sector with high value creation and jobs in Austria (Wettbewerbsfähiger Weltraumsektor)
Ziel 3: Scientific excellence in space and Earth research (Wissenschaftliche Exzellenz)
Ziel 4: Space applications for all areas of life (Weltraum für alle Lebensbereiche)
Ziel 5: Talent and diversity for the space sector (Talente und Diversität)
Ziel 6: A space dialogue with the public (Weltraumdialog mit der Bevölkerung)
strategy.law: Austrian Outer Space Act (Weltraumgesetz; Bundesgesetz über die Genehmigung von Weltraumaktivitäten und die Einrichtung eines Weltraumregisters), BGBl. I No. 132/2011, in force 28 Dec 2011, per the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs record. Implementing Regulation (Weltraumverordnung), BGBl. II No. 36/2015, in force 27 Feb 2015. The official RIS consolidated text was blocked, so later amendments are not verified. No revision in progress was found in this pass.

strategy.title: No single long-term national space strategy document found. Operative instrument: Belgian Space Programming 2026-2030 (Programmation spatiale belge pour la période 2026-2030), Council of Ministers decision of 23 Dec 2025
strategy.horizon: 2026–2030 programming; strategic review of future Belgian space policy by 2028
strategy.owner: Federal Council of Ministers, on the proposal of the Minister for Science Policy (Vanessa Matz); BELSPO implements; Defence co-finances ESA participation
strategy.summary: No single published long-term national space strategy document was found on the BELSPO or federal pages fetched; BELSPO's "Belgian space strategy" page describes policy in general terms. The operative decision is the Council of Ministers programming of 23 Dec 2025 for 2026–2030: it takes note of the November 2025 ESA ministerial, approves the ESA subscriptions and Defence co-financing (EUR 400 million set aside in the multiannual budget), mandates a BELSPO–Defence protocol, and requires a strategic review of future Belgian space policy by 2028 with attention to economic return and regional balance.
strategy.budget: Federal communication (19 Dec 2025): a Belgian contribution of EUR 1.1 billion for the 2026–2030 period. BELSPO debriefing (9 Dec 2025) gives a total Belgian space level of 1,845 M€ for 2025–2030 (1,277 M€ + 168 M€ defence participation + 400 M€ one-off) and about EUR 335 million per year to ESA incl. the defence contribution. Council decision: EUR 400 million set aside in the multiannual budget. Defence: GALO constellation "more than EUR 200 million" (press-reported, 16 Jul 2026; official defence document not found). Defence investment programmes 2026–2034: EUR 617 million (BELSPO deck). Reconciliation of the 1.1 bn and 1,845 M€ figures is not proved.
goals: Fund Belgian subscriptions to the ESA programmes agreed at the November 2025 ministerial (Council decision approves the subscription)
Co-finance Belgian ESA participation with Defence under a BELSPO–Defence protocol, aligned with NATO spending targets where possible (protocol mandated)
Strengthen Belgium's position in ESA's European Resilience from Space programme (mandate to the minister)
Keep ESEC at Redu as ESA's reference centre for cybersecurity (mandate)
Seek more Belgian staff at ESA and a Belgian director post at the next renewal (mandate)
Complete a strategic review of future Belgian space policy by 2028, considering economic return and regional balance
strategy.law: Act of 17 September 2005 on activities of launching, flight operations or guidance of space objects, as consolidated after the revision of 1 December 2013 (Moniteur belge 15 January 2014). It requires authorisation by the Minister for Science Policy and provides for a national registry. Consolidated copy from BELSPO; amendments after 2013 and the status of a draft replacement implementing decree (reported in 2021) were not verified.

strategy.title: Raumfahrtstrategie der Bundesregierung ("Neue Wege für die Raumfahrt")
strategy.status: adopted by cabinet 27 Sep 2023; renewal under review (Drucksache 21/2796, 13 Nov 2025); no newer strategy adopted in fetched sources
strategy.horizon: Not stated in the fetched text
strategy.owner: Federal Government; policy run by BMFTR Department R (space policy and industry, sub-division R1)
strategy.summary: The 2023 national space strategy sets nine priority areas: European and international cooperation with ESA as core framework; space as a high-tech and New Space market; climate, resources and environment; digitalisation and downstream use; security and strategic capacity; sustainable use of outer space; space research; international exploration; and space dialogue and talent. The government said on 13 Nov 2025 that a decision on a new strategy would follow full integration of the BMFTR structures. The first federal space security strategy was presented in cabinet on 19 Nov 2025.
strategy.budget: About EUR 7.5 billion for BMFTR space in this legislative period, stated by the minister in the Bundestag (bulletin 22 Apr 2026, "knapp 7,5 Milliarden Euro in dieser Legislaturperiode"). 2026 government draft space lines (Drucksache 21/2796): BMFTR EUR 137 m; BMWE EUR 1,287 m; BMV EUR 345 m. Draft figures; enacted 2026 budget not checked.
goals: Strengthen European and international cooperation, with ESA as the core framework.
Grow space as a high-tech and New Space market, including launch and small satellite companies.
Use space data for climate, environment, digitalisation and downstream applications.
Secure strategic capacity to act and protect space infrastructure as critical infrastructure.
Promote sustainable use of outer space, including debris mitigation.
Sustain space research, exploration and talent recruitment.
strategy.law: No German space activities act found in force. Cabinet key points (Eckpunkte) for a Weltraumgesetz adopted 4 Sep 2024 (BT-Drs. 20/12775). Per the official lobby register (industry entries of June and 27 Jul 2026), a national space law is in inter-ministerial coordination (Ressortabstimmung); no BMFTR or BMWE draft (Referentenentwurf) was found published as of 27 Oct 2026.

strategy.title: Stratégie nationale spatiale (SNS) 2025-2040
strategy.status: presented (12 Nov 2025); formal adoption instrument and text not located
strategy.horizon: 2040 (per 6 Mar 2025 mandate)
strategy.owner: Prime Minister (mandate, coordinated by the SGDSN with the ministries and CNES); presented by the President
strategy.summary: The Prime Minister mandated the SGDSN on 6 Mar 2025 to draft a national space strategy covering civil and military dimensions to 2040, integrating the 2019 defence space strategy. The President presented the SNS on 12 Nov 2025 at the Space Command in Toulouse as a five-axis action plan, linked to the ESA ministerial conference and a spring 2026 space summit. The formal text (synthèse exécutive) was not found on info.gouv.fr or sgdsn.gouv.fr.
strategy.budget: Presidential announcement (12 Nov 2025, Élysée transcript): more than 16 billion euros for civil space including dual-use activities by 2030, excluding purely military; additional space margins of 4.2 billion euros for 2026-2030 within the military programming law update. Not a budget law or annex; no budget document opened.
goals: Keep France and Europe autonomous access to space
Rethink the industrial and commercial model of space industries
Rethink strategic and defence space capabilities
Adopt a more offensive approach to space science and exploration

strategy.title: UK Space Strategy
strategy.horizon: Spending review period to 2030 with longer-term goals to 2035 (strategy text)
strategy.owner: UK Space Agency, Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and Ministry of Defence (joint publication; BIST and MOD coordinate cross-government framework)
strategy.summary: The UK Space Strategy, published 8 Sep 2026 and updated 15 Sep 2026, sets out the UK approach to space with defence, national security and economic growth at its centre. It is backed by more than £7.8 billion of funding to 2029/30 and has a plan to 2030 under the spending review and goals to 2035. Strategic oversight sits with the Cabinet-level National Security Council; BIST and MOD coordinate a cross-government framework; a ministerially chaired Space Industry Advisory Group was set up in May 2026.
strategy.budget: More than £7.8 billion to 2029/30 (strategy text). Activity envelopes for 26/27 to 29/30 stated in the strategy: SatCom £2.8 billion (including Defence Satellite Communications £2.3 billion); Space Discovery £1.295 billion; Earth observation and meteorology £990 million; Space Ecosystem £706 million (including MOD novel technologies £420 million and National Space Innovation Programme £65 million); Space Domain Awareness £274 million; Assured Access to Space £227 million; in-space servicing, assembly and manufacturing (ISAM) £117 million.
goals: Be a competitive space power, assertive in protecting UK interests and driving growth (strategy vision)
Put defence, national security and economic growth at the centre of the UK approach
Strengthen collective defence through NATO, sharing capabilities and supporting assured access to space
Pro-growth regulation that protects orbital and terrestrial environments and enables safe operations
Scale up commercial space businesses and deliver assured and nationally separable capabilities
By 2035: a leading in-space servicing, assembly and manufacturing (ISAM) industry; assured UK launch access; nationally separable space control and SDA
strategy.law: Space Industry Act 2018 and Outer Space Act 1986 (legislation.gov.uk; both up to date with changes known to be in force on 27 Oct 2026). The CAA administers the Space Industry Act 2018 licensing regime; the Act schedule proves CAA charging, and the annex names the CAA as reforming orbital licensing.

strategy.status: expired (horizon 2025); successor in preparation (DETE, 20 Mar 2026; scoping only)
strategy.owner: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment (then Department of Business, Enterprise and Innovation)
strategy.summary: Ireland national space strategy for enterprise, adopted 2019, aims to grow space-active Irish companies participation in ESA and EU programmes. Fourth progress report (published Mar 2026, covering 2024) says 15 of 19 priority actions are achieved. A fifth and final progress report is under way. DETE said on 20 Mar 2026 that preparatory work has begun on the next iteration with a preliminary scoping exercise, including public consultation. No successor text was found.
strategy.budget: No separate budget line for the 2019-2025 strategy was opened. Irish government ESA allocation EUR 32.17m in 2024 (DETE, 20 Mar 2026). EUR 170m ESA commitment to 2030 agreed at the Council of Ministers in Nov 2025 (DETE, 20 Mar 2026; ESA page says over five years).
goals: Double the space related revenue and employment in space-active Irish companies (by 2025)
Support 100 companies to benefit from ESA engagement (116 achieved by end 2024, per progress report)
Double the value of contracts won through EU Horizon programmes in space-related activities
Increase industry, public and international awareness of space and Ireland activities in space
Develop and attract talent for space-active and related industries
Develop a sustainable Earth Observation services sector based on advanced data analytics
strategy.law: No Irish national space activities law identified in the sources opened. The 2019 strategy assigned the Space Enterprise Coordination Group to consider an appropriate legislative framework; DETE consultation on the EU Space Act (updated 17 Aug 2026) concerns the EU proposal. Absence is NOT confirmed by a current statutory search (see flags); ComReg licensing of satellite earth stations is seed-only.

strategy.title: Documento Strategico di Politica Spaziale Nazionale (DSPSN), National Space Policy Strategic Document
strategy.status: approved by COMINT at its 29th meeting (session 14 May 2026, reported by ASI 15 May 2026); full text not located on the official sites opened
strategy.horizon: Medium to long term (ASI page). The ten-year horizon and 15-year funding reported in press are not verified.
strategy.owner: COMINT (approves), prepared by ASI in coordination with COMINT; COMINT sits at the Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Law 89/2025 Art. 2)
strategy.summary: The COMINT approved the National Space Policy Strategic Document (DSPSN), prepared by ASI, which sets the national strategic framework for the sector in the medium-long term with objectives, priorities and lines of action: security and resilience of space infrastructure; competitiveness of the industrial supply chain; research; skills; strategic autonomy; and Italy’s international projection (ASI, 15 May 2026). It implements the government guidelines on space and aerospace approved in 2025 (ASI wording "lo scorso anno") and sits within Law 89/2025, whose Art. 22 requires a national space economy plan of at least five years, approved by COMINT and updated every two years.
strategy.budget: Statutory: Fondo per l’economia dello spazio, EUR 35 million endowment for 2025 in the MIMIT budget (Law 89/2025 Art. 23). ESA: Italy’s commitment at the ESA Council at Ministerial level 2025 is EUR 3.5 billion over three years, +13.5% on the previous ministerial (ASI Annual Report 2025). Press only (not proved as a primary budget): a government headline of EUR 7.8 billion to 2028 for the space plan, which L’Espresso reports as partly already allocated and spent. PNRR and PNC splits from the seed are not re-proved.
strategy.law: Law No. 89 of 13 June 2025, "Disposizioni in materia di economia dello spazio" (space economy law), Gazzetta Ufficiale Serie generale n. 144 of 24 June 2025, in force the day after publication (Art. 31). It defines ASI and COMINT (by reference to Art. 21 of d.lgs. 128/2003, as amended), creates the national authorisation regime for space activities, the national space economy plan (Art. 22) and the space economy fund (Art. 23). Implementing decrees (Art. 13 and others) were not verified.
goals: Strengthen security and resilience of national space infrastructure (ASI, 15 May 2026)
Increase competitiveness of the industrial supply chain (ASI, 15 May 2026)
Enhance research, develop skills and strengthen strategic autonomy (ASI, 15 May 2026)
Consolidate Italy’s international projection (ASI, 15 May 2026)

strategy.title: Long-Term Space Agenda (Lange-termijn ruimtevaartagenda, LTR)
strategy.horizon: 10–15 years, per the 27 Jan 2026 letter
strategy.owner: Coordinating minister (EZK), with the Stuurgroep NLSA (EZK, OCW, IenW, Defence)
strategy.summary: The LTR, dated January 2024, sets six missions for security and defence capacity, climate and living environment, scientific leadership, satellite data for society, economic opportunities for Dutch companies, and a strong international legal framework. The cabinet response of February 2025 created the Interdepartmental Council for the Space Domain (IRR). A 2017–2024 policy evaluation (completed July 2025) found the missions insufficiently concrete, and the cabinet letter of 27 Jan 2026 commits to prioritising them. The Netherlands Space Office became the Netherlands Space Agency (NLSA) on 3 March 2026. The LTR is a policy framework; no statute was found for it.
strategy.budget: ESA subscriptions for 2026–2028 of EUR 450.3 million at MC25: EUR 167.8 million mandatory and EUR 282.5 million optional, including a one-off EUR 109 million top-up (EUR 85 million from EZK, EUR 24 million from Defence). No separate LTR budget line was opened. The seed's '2.6 percent of the ESA total' is not used because the letter gives a 22.3 billion euro package, which does not support it.
goals: Build security and defence capacity in and through space (LTR mission 1)
Use space for climate and the living environment (LTR mission 2)
Maintain scientific leadership in space research (LTR mission 3)
Apply satellite data to societal challenges (LTR mission 4)
Create economic opportunities for Dutch companies in the space sector (LTR mission 5)
Strengthen the international legal framework for space use (LTR mission 6)
strategy.law: Space Activities Act (Wet ruimtevaartactiviteiten): RDI issues licences for space activities (business.gov.nl). The UN registry holds the English version of the bill dated 13.06.06. The enactment year (2007 in the seed) and current consolidated text were not verified in this run.

strategy.owner: Council of Ministers (approval); implemented by Portugal Space (the agency); MECI leads the ESA delegation
strategy.summary: Portugal Space 2030 was approved by the Council of Ministers on 15 February 2018 with the draft space law. Agency pages fetched on 27 Oct 2026 still describe it as the national space strategy. The 2025–2026 agenda, as shown in government and agency sources, centres on the record ESA subscription, the Santa Maria (Azores) launch and return site, and the Atlantic Constellation with Defence funding. No successor strategy was found in the sources opened in this run.
strategy.budget: No strategy-specific budget was opened. The national ESA subscription for 2026–2030 is EUR 204.8 million, a 51% increase, prepared by the Space Interministerial Working Group (government release, 25 Nov 2025). The Atlantic Constellation resilience component is mainly funded by the Ministry of National Defence (same release).
goals: Raise Portugal's ESA subscription to EUR 204.8 million for 2026–2030 (government release, 25 Nov 2025)
Develop launch and return capability at Santa Maria, Azores, including the Space Rider return site (government release)
Build national Earth observation capability through the Atlantic Constellation (government release)
Regulate access to space activities and launch-centre licensing (Decree-Law 20/2024; Regulation 1206-A/2024)
strategy.law: Decree-Law 16/2019 of 22 January 2019 on access to and exercise of space activities, as amended by Decree-Law 20/2024 of 2 February 2024 (adding launch-centre licensing). Implementing Regulation 1206-A/2024 of 21 October 2024 amends Regulation 697/2019 and confirms ANACOM as Space Authority (Diário da República).

government.notes: Presidential republic: the President is both head of state and head of government. No national space agency, space office, space strategy, space budget or space law was found. A 2022 announcement said the government was building a space agency with a council of ministries; no record of its creation was found. In 27 Feb 2026 the President announced a commercial spaceport in Pedernales (Oviedo) with a US company, investment above US$600 million, and a launch target before May 2028. The Presidency is marked lead:true because it is the only body with a proven role in the current space project; this is lead by practice, not by a legal mandate. Gaceta Oficial and the Chamber of Deputies portal were not reachable, so absence of a decree or law is partial.

government.notes: Falkland Islands: British Overseas Territory. Sovereign side is the Crown (King Charles III), represented by the Governor (FCDO-based office). Local government is the Falkland Islands Government; its own site (falklands.gov.fk) was unreachable, so the Chief Executive is evidenced by FIDC's bio only. No space ministry, agency or office was found; the collective FIG node is lead:true because no distinct lead exists. The UK space institutions (UK Space Agency, DSIT/DBIST) are not proved to apply: the Space Industry Act 2018 extends to the Territory only by Order in Council, and none was found. Head of government is ambiguous: the Territory has no prime minister; the Chief Executive heads the public service.

strategy.title: No Falkland Islands space strategy found; no space policy adopted by the Territory
strategy.summary: No Falkland Islands Government space strategy, office or policy was found. The only space-related item is a private proposal by JETstreaM for satellite ground stations on FIDC-owned land (13 Aug 2026), which had not been approved in the sources opened. Space regulation would come from the UK only if a UK Order in Council extends the Space Industry Act 2018 to the Territory; no such Order was found.
strategy.law: No space law in force in the Falkland Islands was found. The Space Industry Act 2018 extends to England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland (s.71(1)); s.71(5) allows an Order in Council to extend it to British overseas territories; none was found in the sources opened.
other_docs: The Falkland Islands Constitution Order 2008 (SI 2008/2846) sets the Governor, Executive Council and Legislative Assembly; it does not mention space.

A 2009 state programme for a Moldovan microsatellite is documented in a 2013 UTM repository item; its current status is not verified.
